scenes.title: Previously: what an agent is
flow: A model can only produce text
You fetched the files by hand
An agent is a model, tools and a loop

captions.text: Recap of chapter 09: a model can only produce text.
It can't open a file. Something else has to act.
You played that part. The model asked, and you fetched the files.
An agent is a model, tools and a loop. Today, code replaces you.
Today's black box: how a model gets a tool to run.
Let's open it.
This program is provided. Run it first, and we'll open it right after.
The input: one question about Monday, from the sales files you read in chapter 09.
The model didn't answer. It replied with JSON, asking for a tool.
Code ran that tool, and got the real file.
Then the model answered from the result. Nobody fetched anything by hand.
Open the code. Tools are ordinary Python functions.
TOOLS is a dict from a name to a function. The name is text, and text is what a model can write.
The model can't see your Python. So the system message describes each tool.
Your code needs to read the request. First, ask with no schema.
Predict: how many of five replies will be valid JSON?
None of them. The model wrote a sentence around its request, so json.loads can't read it.
So use chapter 08's tool: a schema, passed as format.
The tool must be one of our names. Arguments can be any object.
The same question, with the schema: valid JSON in 5 of 5 runs.
dispatch runs the tool. It looks the name up in TOOLS and calls that function.
The two stars unpack the arguments dict into named arguments.
A failed tool returns text starting with Error. We'll see why soon.
ask is the whole round trip. First call: the model asks for a tool.
Read the JSON, and run the tool.
Add the request and the result to the conversation.
Second call. Models have no memory, so we send it all again.
There's no Sunday file. Predict: will this crash, or will the model make up a number?
The file was missing, so dispatch sent the error back as text.
The model read it and said so. In 5 of 5 runs, it didn't invent a number.
A joke needs no tool. Predict: what will the model ask for?
It asked for a tool anyway, in 5 of 5 runs. The schema requires one.
So this version can't choose to skip tools. Keep that in mind.
One more test: a question no tool fits, with the enum removed.
The model invented a tool called weather, in 5 of 5 runs. dispatch would return an error.
Shape isn't truth. Always check what the model asks for.
Your turn. Open exercises.py and complete the five TODOs.
You've finished when you see 5 passed. The tests use a fake model.
